description: Up to the precedented number of doses, stopping on success. Dominant lever in the graft ablation (-43.50 pp when removed).
Successive doses add rather than replace. Worth +8.85 pp over best-of-k at four doses, and the only operator that can represent the published split-dose result.
A measured signal guides the next dose. Nearly inert once dosing is cumulative (+0.40 pp), so it is a candidate for DROPPING rather than keeping.
A viability-specific signal. Without it feedback is blind and contributes exactly nothing. Adds a second genetic modification to the product.
Re-dose only patients whose pre-dose function leaves room. Up to 2.34x enrichment, using a signal already in the clinic.
The same graft improved 1.77x between three and seventeen months with no extra procedure. The cheapest lever in the whole catalogue.
Scales each increment by the room left. LOWERS the claim. Encodes the ceiling effect measured in the blinded human repeat trial.
Only a third of patients respond to a repeat dose at all. LOWERS the claim. Removing it is what drove ATLAS-4 to a spurious 100%.
